items.content: AlphaFold 3 achieves 76.4% success rate (ligand RMSD < 2.0 Å) in blind protein-ligand docking, significantly outperforming AutoDock Vina (52.1%) and other baseline methods.
items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective), the report computes pocket-aligned ligand RMSD (0.98 ± 0.24 Å for its sequence-frame variant vs. 13.47 Å for the AF3-style baseline and 28.56 Å for random placement), but only by training and evaluating on the exact same single protein-peptide complex (PDB 2L3R) rather than performing blind docking on unseen targets. Crucially, comparisons with AutoDock Vina or other established docking baselines, benchmark success rates (ligand RMSD < 2.0 Å across unseen complexes), statistical significance testing (p < 0.001), and validation across multiple test sets are completely absent, with PoseBusters-style evaluation mentioned only as future work. Although the author transparently acknowledges that single-structure fitting cannot test generalization, evaluating memorization on a single training complex represents a fundamental methodological limitation relative to the paper's blind protein-ligand docking benchmark.

items.content: Visualization of protein-ligand complex predictions showing accurate reproduction of key interactions including hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic contacts, and π-stacking.
items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode B, the report provides only global 2D PCA projections overlaying the predicted and experimental protein Cα traces with unbonded peptide atom scatter points, supplemented by generic <4.5 Å contact counts and pocket-aligned RMSD metrics. It omits protein side chains and binding-pocket close-ups entirely, failing to visualize or verify any of the required chemical interactions—specifically hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic contact areas, and π-stacking within the UHRF1 binding pocket. Moreover, the structure is memorized by training directly on the single target complex (2L3R) and fails to learn sub-1 Å stereochemistry (with Cα chirality remaining at ~50% chance), precluding accurate reproduction of specific non-covalent interactions.

items.reasoning: Under Objective Evaluation (Mode A), the report provides no quantitative accuracy metrics for protein-nucleic acid interactions or antibody-antigen complexes (which are never mentioned), nor does it include any comparisons against specialized predictors. Although the agent implements a unified token/atom diffusion architecture and runs a shape-only forward pass on synthetic DNA/RNA inputs, all reported structural metrics come from fitting and evaluating on the exact same single protein-peptide complex (PDB 2L3R). Because cross-complex generalization and nucleic-acid accuracy are only mentioned as unmeasured limitations without quantitative benchmark results, the criterion is minimally addressed.

items.content: Training convergence curve showing stable learning and rapid convergence of the diffusion model compared to previous architecture.
items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective), the agent provides genuine multi-term training loss curves across 800-1,200 steps, checkpoint reconstruction metrics, and a thorough diffusion sampling-step (10-200 steps) and CPU-runtime optimization sweep, though none of its figures match the target cosine diffusion schedule plot. Crucially, however, all curves reflect overfitting to a single structure (PDB 2L3R) with zero held-out validation performance, unlearned fine-scale stereochemistry (50% random C-alpha chirality), and a failure of the standard AF3-style rotation-augmented diffusion model to converge (~16 A RMSD) without a custom canonical-frame workaround. Furthermore, the report completely omits any empirical convergence or computational efficiency comparison against the previous AlphaFold 2 architecture.

items.content: Ablation studies confirm the importance of diffusion module and PairFormer architecture, with removal of either component resulting in >15% performance degradation.
items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective Evaluation), the report conducts a quantitative Pairformer-lite trunk ablation showing >36% lDDT degradation (0.33 to 0.21) and >140% Cα RMSD worsening (5.28 Å to 12.77 Å), alongside input feature ablations and diffusion sampler/equivariance analyses. However, the study never ablates removing or replacing the diffusion module itself, leaving half of the core architectural criterion untested. Furthermore, the ablation methodology has significant flaws compared to the published paper: all metrics reflect single-structure memorization (training and evaluating on the same 2L3R complex), triangle attention is omitted from the Pairformer, and component ablations are evaluated at an unconverged 200-step warmup checkpoint on a single seed.
